title: Indices, Exponents and Laws of Powers
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Indices, Exponents and Laws of Powers. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Power of a power and product

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Exponent laws

For a nonzero base a, (\(a^m \times a^n=a^{m+n}\)), (\(a^m/a^n=a^{m-n}\)), and (\((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\)). A power distributes across multiplication: (\((ab)^n=a^n b^n\)). It does not distribute across addition: (\((a+b)^n\)) is not generally (\(a^n+b^n\)).

Zero, negative and fractional powers

For nonzero a, (\(a^0=1\)) and (\(a^{-n}=1/a^n\)). A fractional exponent represents a root: (\(a^{1/n}=\sqrt[n]{a}\)). For a real even root, the radicand must be nonnegative. Reduce a rational exponent and check the real-domain restriction. In ordinary school algebra, (\(0^0\)) is undefined.

Scientific notation

Scientific notation writes a nonzero number as (\(a \times 10^n\)), where (\(1 \le |a|<10\)) and n is an integer. It helps compare magnitude and multiply or divide very large and small measurements.

Worked example: (\(16^{3/4}=(\sqrt[4]{16})^3=2^3=8\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Combine powers only when their bases match; combine bases only when exponent laws permit it.
  • Convert negative exponents to reciprocals before comparing magnitude.
  • For a rational exponent, evaluate an exact root first when possible.
  • Apply a power to every factor inside parentheses.
  • Keep the sign outside a power distinct from a negative base: (\(-3^2\))=-9, while (\((-3)^2=9\)).

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• (\(a^m a^n=a^{m+n}\)); (\(a^m/a^n=a^{m-n}\)) for nonzero a.
  • (\((a^m)^n=a^{mn}\)); (\((ab)^n=a^n b^n\)).
  • (\(a^{-n}=1/a^n\)); (\(a^0=1\)) for nonzero a.
  • (\(a^{m/n}=\sqrt[n]{a^m}\)) when the real root exists.
  • Normalize scientific notation so (\(1 \le |a|<10\)).

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Evaluate (\((3^2)^3\div3^4\)).

    1. (\(3\))
    2. (\(9\))
    3. (\(27\))
    4. (\(81\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(9\))

    (\((3^2)^3=3^6\)), and (\(3^6/3^4=3^2=9\)).

  2. Core:

    Which is equal to (\(5^{-2}\))?

    1. (\(-25\))
    2. (\(-1/25\))
    3. (\(1/25\))
    4. (\(25\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(1/25\))

    A negative exponent means reciprocal: (\(5^{-2}=1/5^2=1/25\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Simplify (\(x^7/x^3\)), where x is nonzero.

    1. (\(x^4\))
    2. (\(x^10\))
    3. (\(x^21\))
    4. (\(1/x^4\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x^4\))

    Subtract exponents for the same nonzero base: (\(x^{7-3}=x^4\)).

  4. Standard:

    Evaluate (\(16^{3/4}\)).

    1. (\(4\))
    2. (\(8\))
    3. (\(12\))
    4. (\(16\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(8\))

    The fourth root of 16 is 2, then (\(2^3=8\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Write (\(0.000072\)) in scientific notation.

    1. (\(7.2 \times 10^{-5}\))
    2. (\(7.2 \times 10^{-4}\))
    3. (\(7.2 \times 10^{-6}\))
    4. (\(72 \times 10^{-5}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(7.2 \times 10^{-5}\))

    Move the decimal five places right to get 7.2, so the power is -5: (\(7.2 \times 10^{-5}\)).
